subject: Materials Science
title: Creep: Slow Deformation Under Load
description: A 60-second lesson on Creep: Slow Deformation Under Load.

hook.text: A lead pipe in a medieval church has sagged under its own weight over centuries — that's creep.

buildup.text: Creep is slow, permanent deformation under constant stress — accelerated by high temperature.

discovery.text: Above about 40% of melting temperature, atoms diffuse fast enough to allow time-dependent deformation.

twist.text: Jet turbine blades operate at 85% of their melting point — creep is the primary failure risk.

climax.text: Nickel superalloys with gamma-prime precipitates resist creep at 1,100°C — enabling modern jet engines.

punchline.text: At high temperature, strong materials slowly give in to stress — patience wins.

quiz.question: What is creep?
options: Slow permanent deformation under constant stress at elevated temperature
Elastic deformation that recovers after unloading
